subject: Post-call recap: BrightLayer token economics & pilot options
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightlayer.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: BrightLayer token economics & pilot options

Thanks for taking time today, Samantha — good conversation. Below is a short recap of what we covered, the key numbers you shared, and a recommended low-risk pilot path that focuses on cost predictability and validating batching/caching levers. Please flag anything I missed.

1) Main pain points you described
- Inference spend variability month-to-month (spikes during feature launches).
- Need to hit p95 latency < 250ms for user-facing flows.
- Budget target: ~USD 8k/month for core inference (current run-rate exceeds this during spikes).
- Concern about quality impact if we switch to smaller/quantized models.

2) Representative token profile (your data)
- Average user request: ~350 tokens input (context + prompt) and ~150 tokens output = ~500 tokens per call.
- Peak QPS during launches ~4–6x normal; steady-state target ~3k–4k calls/day for the pilot cohort.

3) Where we can influence unit economics (short summary)
- Batching: If requests can accept small added latency (~15–30ms), batching reduces GPU overhead and can lower per-call compute cost. Based on similar workloads, effective token amortization improvements of ~1.5x–2.0x are realistic depending on request mix.
- Caching (prefix + session KV): We saw 20%–40% reduction in token generation on comparable customers by caching deterministic prompts and reranking results for repeat queries.
- Model variants / quantization: Moving from FP16 to 4-bit int or using a lower-parameter model variant can reduce inference cost ~30%–50% depending on accuracy tolerance; we can run A/B checks to quantify end-user impact.
- Smart routing: We can route low-acuity requests to a cheaper variant and high-value requests to the higher-quality model, which preserves UX while lowering blended cost.

4) Quick back-of-envelope monthly example (estimate for discussion only)
- Baseline: 3k calls/day * 30 days * 500 tokens = 45M tokens/month.
- If caching = 30% effective token reduction => 31.5M billable tokens.
- If batching + quantization together reduce effective cost per token by ~40% => blended spend could fall roughly in-line with your $8k/month target (final number depends on exact model pricing and batch factors).

5) Proposed pilot (goal: prove cost & latency with measurable levers)
- Duration: 4 weeks (2-week ramp, 2-week steady-state validation).
- Scope: ~100k total calls (sampling across your three primary user flows), verify p95 latency target and measure token reductions from caching and batching.
- Deliverables: token burn dashboard, per-route cost breakdown, latency heatmaps, and an ROI brief tying cost reduction to MAU economics.
- Cost/contract: We can run the pilot under hosted credits for the first 2 weeks; after that, a short paid pilot/PO for the remainder (I attached a one-pager and a simple token model spreadsheet).

6) Risks & mitigations
- Quality regression from quantization: we’ll run parallel A/B tests and provide evaluation metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-style or task-specific metrics you prefer).
- Burst capacity: use autoscale + policy-based fallback to cheaper model variants during launch spikes to prevent cost overruns.

Next steps
- You confirm pilot scope (sample flows + dataset slice) — due Mon 3/30.
- I’ll send a short pilot statement of work and a recommended config for batching/caching to your engineering team by Tue 3/31.
- Schedule technical deep-dive with your infra/ML team (30–45m) — suggested times Wed 3/31 or Thu 4/1.

Attachments: brightlayer_pilot_one_pager.pdf, brightlayer_token_model.xlsx

Thanks again — happy to tighten the numbers after you share the sample request logs.

Best,
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightlayer.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: BrightLayer token economics & pilot options

Thanks Logan — this is really helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from my side: 
- The $8k/month target is for the user-facing inference layer only (we have separate infra/embedding costs).
- For the pilot we can provide a 2-week request log sample (anonymized) covering our three flows: onboarding prompts, in-app completions, and scheduled batch summaries.
- Important: we need to preserve model output fidelity for onboarding flows (we can tolerate a tiny increase in hallucination rate for batch summaries but not for onboarding).

Can you include a short example batching configuration (batch window, max batch size, expected added latency) in the SOW? Diego and I also want to see how prefix caching would be implemented (session keys, TTL recommendations).

I’m available Wed 3/31 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 4/1 13:00–14:00 PT for the technical deep-dive. We’ll loop in one infra engineer (procure@brightlayer.ai) and our Head of ML Ops. Also, can you confirm whether you can run the first 2 weeks entirely on hosted credits? That helps us get internal approval.

Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Product, BrightLayer
samantha@brightlayer.ai
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightlayer.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: BrightLayer token economics & pilot options

Great — thanks for the quick reply and the availability. Short answers:
- We can cover the first 2 weeks on hosted credits — I’ll note that in the SOW.
- I’ll include a sample batching config in the SOW: suggested batch window 20ms–50ms, max batch size 16–32 depending on request shape, expected added tail latency ~10–35ms. We’ll provide a conservative and an aggressive profile so you can choose tradeoffs.
- Prefix/session caching: we’ll propose a TTL strategy (default 5–15 minutes for session caches, longer for deterministic prompts) and include how we compute cache keys (user_id + prompt_hash + context_version).

Next steps I’ll action today:
1) Draft SOW + pilot config w/ two sample batching profiles and caching TTLs — target Tue 3/31 EOD.
2) Add exact token/billing estimates once you share the anonymized logs.
3) Book technical deep-dive for Wed 3/31 10:00 PT (tentatively) and share an invite.

I’ll also attach the HubSpot deal link and the one-pager in the SOW email. If anything else pops up, ping me directly.

Thanks — looking forward to it.
Logan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
